CD PROJEKT RED replied to me about The Witcher 3 and Linux, flat-out denying to answer any questions

It's obvious to any developer that there simply would not be enough profit (if any) to justify porting a AAA game to Linux. The logical choice for any commercial developer is to ignore any platform that has a bad return on investment. At the time Witcher 3 was first announced (Feb 2013), Valve was attempting to tout SteamOS (released Dec 2013) as the next big thing. The killer software which would turn a PC in to a dedicated console-like game system with the software library and all the power of a Windows PC. Unfortunately by all reasonable points of measure SteamOS has proven itself a failure, and Valve has vastly overestimated their chances of success. Linux in all its flavors still has an incredibly poor market share on steam. According to the August Steam hardware survey, Linux accounts for 0.83% of steam users. Even OSX destroys it with 3.34%, while Windows holds 95.71%.

My guess is that CDPR initially drank the koolaid and wanted to be on the hype train early in case it took off. It didn't, so they just threw the plans out rather than take the financial hit. The truth is these are companies who's goal is to make money. Never think they make games just so you can play them, or that they're providing you with services to further some greater good. There's always a profit motive.
